B.rest_w_source: card 1's tile-loop idle median 33.29 W (the dataset); E190 arm B's rests 29.8-31.2 W: a high-side rest

arms_used.gemmL<MB>x<NB>x<KB>: SP_GEMM_LARGE: C (MB x NB blocks of 1,024 x 512) = A (MB x KB blocks) x B (KB x NB blocks); K a block 512 (fp32), 1,024 (fp16), 2,048 (int8); ops a minion a pass MB NB 2 KB 32
arms_used.gemmc1 / gemmc8s / gemmc16s: the line-cost law's arms (rgm107's run_gemm, in the same binary): one block; 8 blocks, C shared; 16 blocks, C shared

kernel.binary: tools/claims-v3/e136/rgm136 (E136's, unchanged; E146, E158, E159, E168, E169 and E190 ran it)
kernel.grid: M a multiple of 1,024, N of 512, K of 32 k tiles; below that only by a shire subset; no epilogue in the kernel
kernel.kernel_elf_pin: aace138c... (E136's build record; aifoundry2's and aifoundry1's builds byte-identical, E190's kit)
kernel.kernel_text_pin: 61315bf6... (E190's KIT.md); arm A's box builds with aifoundry3's RISC-V GCC '(g1b306039a) 15.1.0', whose ELF differs in its version string (E191's verifier, CONTEXT 113): the kit gates arm A's kernel on its .text
kernel.shire_subsets: --shires <mask> --per-shire 32 (the host refuses a GEMM with fewer than 32 minions a shire): shire s computes rows 128 (s >> 2) .. +128 and columns 128 (s & 3) .. +128 of every C block; the same per-minion work, a smaller GEMM on fewer minions
kernel.why_this_kernel: the dataset's GEMM points by kernel: rgm136's gemmL 363 (E136, E146, E158, E159, E168, E169, E190) against the 1-16 block walks of rgm/rgm105/rgm107 (622; 1,024 x 512 blocks only); E190's is the only GEMM kernel ever run on card 1; every shape is an argument; the law's anchor arms are in the same binary

never_run_design.method: each point's (arm string, M, N, K, format, minions) against the 985 GEMM points of OUT/mm-data (GitHub main ce94a428, 12 experiments, every data dir the lab committed); the registration repeats the search over every data dir of ours

planning_vs_e190_card1.what: the planning law's cycles an op beside E190's measured 8,192^3 GEMMs on card 1 at 600 MHz (the dataset): the law's point is slow where strict LRU calls every line fresh (E190's own S8 NONE), its fast end fast; the registration's forecasts carry their own bands
